headline: Oil falls on Iran talks, while tech drags the Nasdaq and the Dow climbs back above 50,000
paragraphs: Oil came under pressure as traders weighed progress in US–Iran negotiations. Brent settled at about US$91.40 a barrel on Tuesday and slipped below US$90 in Asian trading on Wednesday. A deal that brings more Iranian barrels back to market would loosen supply, so the market is trimming some of the risk premium it had built in.

On Wall Street the picture was split. The Dow rose about 0.9% to close at 50,019, back above the 50,000 mark, as investors rotated into value stocks. The S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq led declines with a 1.5% drop as doubts over AI spending weighed on big tech. Investors don't seem to be leaving equities; they are rethinking how much they will pay for growth.
